subject: Science (GCSE Biology, Chemistry, Physics)
source: Seeded from gcse-science/y10 lesson 27 (Respiration comparison table and yeast data sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 27: Respiration: ATP, aerobic and anaerobic. To understand how aerobic and anaerobic respiration release energy as ATP

model.title: A sprinter breathes heavily for 5 minutes after a race. Explain why. [3 marks]

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: During the sprint, muscles respire anaerobically as oxygen supply is too slow

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: After the race extra oxygen is needed to break down the lactic acid

parts.label: Step 4
parts.text: So breathing rate and depth stay high until it is removed

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: Extra oxygen is needed to remove lactic acid built up by anaerobic respiration.

head: Aerobic
Anaerobic
rows: Releases a lot of energy (about 30 ATP per glucose)
Releases far less energy (2 ATP per glucose)

questions.q: Write the balanced symbol equation for aerobic respiration. [2 marks]
questions.model: Reactants: glucose C₆H₁₂O₆ and oxygen O₂. Products: CO₂ and H₂O. Balance carbon: 6CO₂. Hydrogen: 6H₂O. Oxygen: 6 + 12 = 18 on the right, so 6O₂ on the left (6 in glucose + 12 = 18).

questions.q: Word equation for anaerobic respiration in yeast (plants).
Word equation for anaerobic respiration in muscles.
Core: Plot the yeast data (bubbles per minute against temperature) and describe the trend.
questions.a: Rises to a peak at 40 °C (55 per minute) then falls to 0 at 60 °C.
questions.model: Teacher plots 20 °C at 14 and 30 °C at 32 and describes: as temperature rises, rate increases.

questions.q: Extend: Explain the shape of the graph using enzymes. [4 marks]
questions.a: Rate rises as enzymes and substrate gain kinetic energy (1), more collisions (1); above the optimum the enzymes' active sites change shape (1), enzymes denature so rate falls to zero (1).

questions.q: Stretch: Explain why anaerobic respiration releases less energy per glucose. [2 marks]
questions.a: Glucose is only partly broken down (1); much energy remains in lactic acid or ethanol (1).

questions.q: Products of anaerobic respiration in yeast?
Big question: why do your muscles burn when you sprint, and why does bread rise?
questions.a: Muscles respire anaerobically making lactic acid; yeast respires anaerobically making carbon dioxide gas that raises dough.
